Subject: One early iron digging HOE laid low on its side. ANATOMY IS CRITICAL: the wooden haft runs diagonally from upper-right to lower-left and ends in a narrow dark iron gooseneck which bends downward a clear right angle, then turns into a wide shallow rectangular soil blade extending ACROSS the handle axis. Show the top plane of this broad transverse blade as a narrow trapezoid, with its straight cutting edge running horizontally left-right near the lower-left. This is a farming hoe, not an axe: no axe wedge, no axe blade in the handle plane. One plain honey-brown wooden handle, one dark-grey bent iron head. Low wide composition, primitive practical tool, no modern rubber, no factory fittings.
